cohort: Women enrolled in the Slone Birth Defects Study (1976-2015), with those with cNMD (n=125) matched to those without cNMD by interview year and study site
finding: Women with cNMD were more likely to deliver preterm and have an SGA infant.
mod_finding: Women with congenital neuromuscular disabilities (cNMD) were more likely to have a cesarean section.
gest_age: Infants of women with cNMD had shorter gestational length (mean difference: -7.44 days, 95% CI: -13.94, -0.95) compared to women without cNMD
